skill.name: zendesk-automation
skill.description: Automate Zendesk tickets, users, organizations, and replies through Rube MCP with schema-aware tool discovery.
skill.summary: Use Rube MCP to manage Zendesk support workflows from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around Rube and Zendesk tool names. The external Rube MCP endpoint is a real low-severity network dependency, and semantic review found high-impact Zendesk actions that need confirmation controls.

remediation.issue: Ticket deletion is permanent and irreversible.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before delete operations and prefer closing tickets when deletion is not required.

remediation.issue: User creation can include agent, admin, and verified account fields.
remediation.suggestion: Require least-privilege Zendesk scopes and explicit approval before creating elevated or verified users.

remediation.issue: Public replies may email customers by default.
remediation.suggestion: Ask the user to confirm public visibility and recipient impact before sending ticket replies.

remediation.issue: Zendesk operations depend on the external Rube MCP endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Document the third-party trust boundary and verify that the organization approves Rube MCP before use.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Zendesk connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `zendesk`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- LIST uses `page`/`per_page` pagination, NOT offset-based; check `next_page` in response
- Maximum 100 results per page; iterate with page numbers until `next_page` is null
- `description`: Ticket body (for creation; becomes first comment)
- Use `safe_update` with `updated_stamp` to prevent concurrent modification conflicts
- `description` is only used on creation; use REPLY_ZENDESK_TICKET to add comments after creation
- `public`: Boolean; true for public reply, false for internal note
- `author_id`: Author user ID (defaults to authenticated user)
- Set `public: false` for internal notes visible only to agents
- `query`: Search string (matches name, email, phone, etc.)
- Check `next_page` URL in response; null means last page
- Use `safe_update: true` with `updated_stamp` (ISO 8601) to prevent conflicts
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
3. Use user ID as assignee_id in ticket creation/update

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Zendesk Ticket Deletion Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents ZENDESK_DELETE_ZENDESK_TICKET and warns that ticket deletion is permanent and irreversible. An agent following an unconfirmed request could destroy support records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple lines explicitly expose delete-ticket tooling and describe deletion as unrecoverable. The business-impact risk is direct even though the capability may be legitimate for authorized admins.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Zendesk Role Elevation Through User Creation
semantic_findings.description: The skill can create Zendesk users and includes role values for end-user, agent, and admin, plus a verified flag. Misuse could provision elevated accounts if the connected credentials allow it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The role and verified parameters are documented clearly, but actual privilege changes depend on Zendesk plan settings and OAuth scopes.

semantic_findings.title: Public Ticket Replies Can Send Customer Email
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents public ticket replies and notes that the default public reply sends email to the requester. Accidental or malicious use could disclose information or send unauthorized messages.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly describes public replies and requester email behavior. The risk is contextual because authorized support teams may need this function.

content.value_statement: Zendesk work often requires repeated ticket, user, and organization steps across several screens. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows with current schemas.
actual_capabilities: Searches Rube MCP for current Zendesk tool schemas before action.
Lists and retrieves Zendesk tickets with page-based pagination guidance.
Creates, updates, replies to, and deletes Zendesk tickets through documented tool sequences.
Searches and creates Zendesk users, including requester and assignee lookup steps.
Lists, retrieves, creates, updates, and counts Zendesk organizations.
Documents safe update, tag replacement, and rate limit behavior for Zendesk workflows.
limitations: Requires an active Rube MCP connection and authenticated Zendesk access.
Does not include executable scripts or direct Zendesk API client code.
Tool schemas may change, so it requires Rube tool discovery before each workflow.
Destructive actions depend on the permissions of the connected Zendesk account.

use_cases.title: Ticket Queue Triage
use_cases.description: List, filter, and inspect support tickets while respecting Zendesk pagination and ticket detail limits.

use_cases.title: Customer Response Drafting
use_cases.description: Retrieve ticket state and add a public reply or internal note with the correct visibility setting.

use_cases.title: Account Data Maintenance
use_cases.description: Find users, create records, and manage organization details through repeatable Zendesk tool sequences.

prompt_templates.title: List Recent Tickets
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Zendesk automation skill to list recent tickets. Search Rube tools first, then show status, priority, requester, and next page availability.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Support Ticket
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Zendesk ticket for this customer issue. Search users first, confirm the requester, then create the ticket with priority, type, and tags.

prompt_templates.title: Reply With Visibility Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a reply for ticket 12345. Get the current ticket first, ask me to confirm public or internal visibility, then post the reply.

prompt_templates.title: Update Ticket Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Update ticket 12345 without overwriting newer changes. Retrieve the ticket, preserve existing tags, use safe_update with updated_stamp, and report any conflict.

output_examples.input: Show me high-priority open tickets from Zendesk.
output_examples.output: A concise ticket list with ticket IDs, subjects, priorities, statuses, requester names, and whether another page is available.

output_examples.input: Add an internal note to ticket 4821 about the refund review.
output_examples.output: Confirmation that the ticket was retrieved first, the note was marked internal, and the update was posted to the selected ticket.

output_examples.input: Create an organization for Acme Support with the acme.example domain.
output_examples.output: A creation summary with organization name, domain, any tags or notes used, and follow-up checks for duplicate names.

best_practices: Search Rube tools before every workflow so the latest Zendesk schema is used.
Fetch current records before updates to preserve tags and avoid stale writes.
Confirm visibility, deletion, and elevated user roles before performing high-impact actions.
anti_patterns: Do not delete tickets when closing or solving the ticket would meet the request.
Do not post public replies until the user confirms customer-facing visibility.
Do not replace tags without first merging the existing tag list.

faq.question: Does this skill require Zendesk credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires an active Zendesk connection through Rube MCP before workflows can run.

faq.question: Can it run without Rube MCP?
faq.answer: No. The skill is written for the Rube MCP Zendesk toolkit and its tool schemas.

faq.question: Does it include executable code?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown workflow guide for AI tools that can call Rube MCP.

faq.question: Can it delete Zendesk tickets?
faq.answer: Yes, if the connected account has permission. Deletion should require explicit confirmation because it is irreversible.

faq.question: Why does it search tools first?
faq.answer: Rube tool schemas can change. Searching first helps the assistant use current parameters and avoid stale calls.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported clients for this skill.
